name: Findias
sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: The entry for Findias concerns Find, a divinity of Ireland. This word, meaning white, turns up within the names of many mythic figures and heroes of folk tale. Evidence hints at an early deity with this name, perhaps a god who came before the great hero Fionn Mac Cumhaill, alternatively a goddess tied to Bóand, a white cow goddess who gave her name to the River Boyne. Later, the geographer Ptolemy spoke of a deity he called Bouvinda during the second century of the Common Era, whose name shares a root with the magic cow Bó Find, a creature that may itself appear as an aspect of Bóand. One cannot say whether the term functions as a name or merely a title, or whether it points to one being or to the shining quality of divinity at large.
